scope: employer of a worker; not stated; drilling incident with possible asbestos exposure, worker without a mask
rules: Where a worker may have been exposed to asbestos fibres in an incident, including working without proper respiratory protection, the exposure must be noted on their health record, or on their personal file if they have no health record.
An incident that releases asbestos fibres should itself be recorded.

scope: plumbing firm; not stated; removing old pipe lagging in an airing cupboard
rules: Removing or disturbing asbestos pipe lagging is licensable work that only a contractor holding an HSE licence may do.
Pipe lagging is a high-risk material because it releases fibres very easily, and wearing masks does not make the work non-licensed.

scope: not stated; not stated; drilling holes in a vinyl floor tile for a pipe
rules: Drilling a hole in an asbestos floor tile is lower-risk non-licensed work, so no licence is needed.
Maintenance work on vinyl or thermoplastic floor tiles is normally not notifiable, but workers still need non-licensed asbestos training and suitable controls.

scope: contractor; not stated; notifiable non-licensed asbestos work in tenants' flats
rules: For notifiable non-licensed asbestos work in domestic premises and on construction sites, the enforcing authority is HSE; local authorities enforce in premises such as shops, offices and hotels.

scope: contractor; not stated; removing textured coating strips in 30 flats on one estate over three months
rules: A programme of several notifiable non-licensed asbestos jobs in one local area, such as a housing estate, can be notified once for the whole programme instead of job by job.

scope: employer; not stated; workers doing notifiable non-licensed asbestos work
rules: For each worker doing notifiable non-licensed asbestos work, the employer must keep a health record (register) giving the type and duration of asbestos work, the estimated exposure and the dates of medical examinations.
The health record must be kept for 40 years.
The record can be as simple as noting the workers' names on the kept copy of the notification.

scope: employer; not stated; workers using disposable masks on asbestos jobs
rules: Tight-fitting respiratory facepieces, including disposable masks, must be face fit tested by a competent person when first selected, for the exact model and size the worker uses.
The fit test must be repeated when the mask model or size changes or the wearer's face changes significantly, such as weight change or dental work.
Wearers of tight-fitting masks must be clean-shaven where the mask seals.

scope: not stated; not stated; reoccupation of a tenanted flat after licensed asbestos removal
rules: After licensed asbestos work indoors, the area must pass a four-stage clearance (site completion check, detailed visual inspection inside the enclosure, air test, final check after the enclosure is removed) before a reoccupation certificate is issued; the air test is skipped for outdoor work.
The clearance must be carried out by an independent analyst accredited to ISO 17025.

scope: not stated (client or contractor); not stated; clearance after licensed asbestos removal
rules: Until 25 November 2027 the licensed removal contractor may appoint the accredited analyst for the clearance, although guidance strongly recommends the building client appoints the analyst.
From 25 November 2027 the employer responsible for the cleaning must not appoint the person who assesses the area for the reoccupation certificate.
From 25 November 2027 that assessor must be accredited to both ISO 17020 and ISO 17025.

scope: not stated; not stated; changes to the asbestos rules in 2026 and 2027
rules: The 2026 amendments to the asbestos rules mostly come into force on 25 November 2026, but the provisions starting then only update references to other laws.
The ban on the cleaning employer appointing the clearance assessor starts only on 25 November 2027, and the old rules apply until then.

scope: contractor; not stated; work inside housing association flats
rules: The duty to manage asbestos does not extend to the inside of private domestic flats.
Before work that may disturb asbestos, the employer must find out whether asbestos is present or presume that it is and act on that presumption.

scope: contractor; England (implied); kitchen refit in a home with no existing extractor
rules: When work is done in a kitchen, existing extract fans and cooker hoods venting outside should be kept or replaced.
If the kitchen had no ventilation system before, one need not be added, unless the work makes the home less compliant with the ventilation requirements than before.
Replacing an extractor fan or cooker hood on the existing cabling does not need to be notified to building control.

scope: contractor; England (implied); replacing all windows in an existing 1930s semi-detached house
rules: Replacement windows in an existing dwelling should achieve a U-value of 1.4 W/m2K or better, or a Window Energy Rating of Band B or better.
Replacement windows should be no worse in energy performance than the ones they replace.

scope: contractor; England (implied); single storey rear extension with large glazed doors and roof lanterns
rules: Under the simple elemental approach, the total area of windows, roof windows, rooflights and doors in an extension should not exceed 25% of the extension floor area plus the area of windows and doors lost or covered by the extension.

More glazing is allowed if the area-weighted U-value of the whole extension is shown to be no worse than a compliant extension of the same size, or a SAP calculation shows the home is no worse than with a notional extension.

scope: contractor; England (implied); kitchen extension over a public sewer
rules: Building over or within 3 m of a sewer shown on the sewer map needs a full plans application; a building notice cannot be used.
The sewerage undertaker that owns a public sewer must be consulted, and its permission is needed to build over or within 3 m of a sewer deeper than 3 m or larger than 225 mm diameter.

Unless the owner agrees, the length of sewer under the building should not exceed 6 m, and a manhole on a sewer serving more than one property should not be built over without other access being agreed.

scope: installer; England (implied); new gas boiler in a home kitchen
rules: When a new or replacement fixed gas appliance, other than one used only for cooking, is installed in a dwelling, a carbon monoxide alarm should be fitted in the same room.

The alarm should meet BS EN 50291-1 and be battery powered with a battery lasting the alarm's life and an end-of-life warning, or a hard-wired mains Type A alarm with a sensor failure warning, not a plug-in.
The alarm should be on the ceiling at least 300 mm from any wall, or high on a wall but not within 150 mm of the ceiling, and between 1 m and 3 m from the appliance.

scope: builder; England; 5 m single storey rear extension to a semi-detached house
rules: For a house that is not detached, a single storey rear extension is permitted development up to 3 m beyond the original rear wall and up to 4 m high.

Outside protected land and SSSIs it can extend up to 6 m only through the prior approval (neighbour consultation) process, and work cannot start until the council says approval is not needed, grants it, or 42 days pass without a decision.
Permitted development does not remove the need for building regulations approval.

scope: builder; England (implied); removing a chimney breast in a terraced house
rules: Removing a chimney breast affects the structure and may need building regulations approval.
Cutting away a chimney breast on a party wall needs a party structure notice served on the neighbour at least two months before the work starts, separately from building regulations.

scope: builder; England (implied); reusing reclaimed bricks in new extension walls
rules: Building work must use adequate and proper materials, which need not be new.
A material's fitness for purpose can be shown by past experience such as successful use in an existing building, or by tests, calculations or certification.

scope: contractor; England (implied); replacement windows in an existing old house
rules: The requirement for doors and windows to resist unauthorised access applies only to new dwellings, including those formed by a material change of use, not to replacement windows in an existing house.

scope: builder; England (implied); timber cladding on a two storey house extension
rules: The ban on combustible materials in external walls applies only to relevant buildings: those with a storey at least 18 m above ground level that contain dwellings, an institution or residential rooms.
An external wall outside the ban must still meet the general fire safety requirements for external walls.

scope: not stated; not stated; a staircase (type and building not stated)
rules: For a stair in a dwelling, each rise should be 150 to 220 mm and each going 220 to 300 mm, with a maximum pitch of 42 degrees.
Headroom over a dwelling stair should be at least 2 m, with a reduced headroom allowed for loft conversions.

scope: responsible person or landlord; England (implied); three-monthly fire door checks in a block of flats
rules: The three-monthly fire door checks are simple visual checks needing no tools, which caretakers, housing officers, managing agents or maintenance staff can do once shown how; no certified specialist is needed.
Repairs or replacements the checks identify must be carried out promptly by a competent contractor.
The routine checks do not replace periodic inspection of doors by fire specialists as part of the fire risk assessment.

scope: council landlord; England (implied); flat front doors in blocks of flats
rules: In a building with two or more sets of domestic premises, fire safety law covers the structure, the external walls, the common parts and all doors between the flats and the common parts.
The person responsible for the communal parts must carry out the fire door checks, and flat entrance doors count as common parts for this purpose.

scope: developer or contractor; England (implied); new block of flats about 13 m high
rules: Sprinklers are recommended in any block of flats with a top storey more than 11 m above ground.

Increasing the fire resistance of walls between flats beyond the recommended level is not an alternative to sprinklers, because it gives little benefit to occupants and none to those in the flat on fire.

scope: council or contractor; England; refurbishment of common parts in a council block (material alteration)
rules: The duty to hand over fire safety information on completion applies only to work that erects or extends a relevant building or forms part of a relevant change of use, not to a material alteration.
After the works, the responsible person must review the fire risk assessment.

scope: social landlord; England; significant hazard in a family's home not made safe in time
rules: If a significant hazard is not made safe within 5 working days (or an emergency hazard within 24 hours), the landlord must arrange suitable alternative accommodation at no cost to the household until the safety work is done, unless the tenant refuses it.
Whether the accommodation is suitable depends on the household's needs, such as number of bedrooms, distance to school and work, disability or medical needs, pets and the length of stay.

scope: social landlord; England; investigations of damp, mould and other hazards
rules: Hazard investigations under the social housing hazard rules do not require an HHSRS assessment, so the investigator needs no HHSRS qualification.

The investigator must be someone the landlord reasonably believes has the skills and experience to judge whether a significant or emergency hazard is present, with a suitably qualified person used where relevant, such as an electrician for an electrical hazard.

scope: landlord; England; re-letting an empty home with a three-year-old electrical report
rules: The electrical inspection before a new tenancy counts as done if an inspection was carried out in the previous 5 years and the report's next-due date has not yet passed.
The new tenant must be given a copy of the latest electrical inspection report before moving in.

scope: social landlord; England; flood from a tenant's own washing machine
rules: The landlord's repairing duty does not cover items the tenant is entitled to remove, such as their own washing machine, appliances that use the water or electricity supply, or repairs due to the tenant's duty to use the home in a tenant-like way.
The landlord's repairing duty still covers damage to the structure, and the hazard rules can apply if a building defect results in a significant or emergency hazard.

scope: landlord; England; tenant's claim that a flat is unfit for human habitation
rules: A landlord must keep the home fit for human habitation at the start of and throughout the tenancy, including common parts in which the landlord has an interest.

Fitness is judged on repair, stability, freedom from damp, internal layout, natural light, ventilation, water supply, drainage and toilets, facilities for preparing food and washing up, and any HHSRS hazard; no formal HHSRS assessment is required.
The duty does not cover problems caused by the tenant, damage by fire or flood, the tenant's own belongings, or work needing consent the landlord could not get despite reasonable efforts.

scope: social landlord; England (implied); tenant reports heating off
rules: Total loss of heating in cold weather where a vulnerable person lives is treated as an emergency hazard, to be made safe within 24 hours.
A home that cannot be kept warm enough can be a significant hazard, and the rules apply only where the heating system is the landlord's to repair.

scope: council landlord; England (implied); mould in a flat's bathroom
rules: An isolated patch of mould over a shower in a home with no vulnerable occupants is outside the hazard rules and is normal maintenance.
Widespread mould where occupants are vulnerable or have symptoms can be a significant or emergency hazard.

scope: contractor; UK; CIS monthly return and payment for the tax month ending 5 December
rules: The monthly CIS return must reach HMRC within 14 days of the end of the tax month, so by the 19th.

CIS deductions paid electronically must reach HMRC within 17 days of the end of the tax month (the 22nd, or the banking day before if that is not a working day), or within 14 days if paid by post or cheque.

scope: company with two directors; UK; applying for CIS gross payment status
rules: For gross payment status a company must show construction turnover, excluding VAT and materials, over the past 12 months of at least £30,000 per director or £100,000 for the company; a company controlled by five or fewer people needs £30,000 per person.
The applicant must also pass the business test (construction work in the UK, run through a bank account) and the compliance test (tax and National Insurance paid on time).

scope: contractor; UK; CIS changes from 6 April 2026
rules: From 6 April 2026 mainstream contractors must again file a nil monthly return for months with no subcontractor payments, unless they told HMRC in advance.
From 6 April 2026 payments to local authorities and listed public bodies are not contract payments, so they need no verification, deduction or reporting.

From 6 April 2026 anti-fraud rules make a business liable where it knew or should have known of deliberate non-compliance in the supply chain, with penalties up to 30%, immediate loss of gross payment status and a five-year wait before reapplying.

scope: contractor working for a property investment company; UK; refurbishment of let flats costing about £3.5m a year
rules: A business outside construction becomes a deemed contractor once its construction spending exceeds £3 million in a rolling 12-month period.
The exemption for work on a business's own premises does not cover property held for letting or as an investment.

scope: builder; UK; building a granny annexe that cannot be sold separately from the main house
rules: An annexe that cannot be lived in or disposed of separately from the main house does not meet the 'designed as a dwelling' conditions, so its construction is not zero-rated and is standard-rated at 20%.

scope: contractor working for a developer; UK; converting an office block into four flats
rules: Converting non-residential premises such as offices into dwellings, or changing the number of dwellings, is a qualifying conversion charged at the reduced 5% rate.
Such a conversion is zero-rated only when done for a relevant housing association.

scope: contractor or subcontractor; England and Wales (implied); sub-contract with no payment terms
rules: Where a construction contract of 45 days or more has no payment terms, interim payments fall due on the later of 7 days after the end of each period (28 days if no period is set) and the payee's claim.
The final date for payment is 17 days after the due date.
The final payment falls due 30 days after completion or the payee's claim, whichever is later.

scope: contractor; UK (implied); four-week construction contract with a subcontractor
rules: A party to any construction contract, however short, has the right to refer a dispute to adjudication.
The 45-day duration only decides whether a party is entitled to stage payments; contracts with a residential occupier are excluded from the statutory rights.

scope: contractor; England; district council works contract worth about £180,000
rules: For a regulated contract below the threshold, an authority inviting tenders must not use a separate suitability assessment stage, such as financial or technical pre-qualification, to filter bidders.
That ban does not apply to works contracts at or above £207,720 for local authorities (£135,018 for central government), and the authority may still consider suitability when assessing tenders.

scope: contractor; UK; bidding for central government contracts over £5 million a year
rules: Bidders for central government contracts worth more than £5 million a year must show effective supply chain payment systems, meeting a standard of 95% of invoices paid within 60 days.

scope: contractor; UK; paying a new subcontractor under CIS
rules: A contractor must verify a subcontractor with HMRC before paying them for the first time, using their UTR, NI number or company details and registered name.
The deduction is 20% for a registered subcontractor, 30% if unregistered or not matched, and nothing if they have gross payment status.
The deduction applies only to the labour part of the payment, after excluding the subcontractor's materials, hired plant and VAT.

scope: builder; UK; a house job (type of work not stated)
rules: Building work on existing buildings is normally standard-rated at 20%.

Building a new dwelling can be zero-rated; converting non-residential premises into homes or changing the number of dwellings is usually 5%, and renovating a home empty for at least 2 years can be 5%.

scope: builder as the only contractor; Great Britain (implied); kitchen extension for a homeowner
rules: A homeowner having work done on their own home, not in connection with a business, is a domestic client.
On a domestic project with only one contractor, the client duties pass to that contractor in addition to its own contractor duties.

scope: principal contractor; Great Britain (implied); homeowner project with an architect
rules: A domestic client may agree in writing for the principal designer to carry out the client duties.
Without that written agreement, the client duties pass to the principal contractor, even if the designer coordinates the project.

scope: contractor; Great Britain (implied); refurbishing housing association flats
rules: Housing associations, councils, landlords and other businesses that own homes are not domestic clients; they are commercial clients and carry the client duties in full.
Only a person having work done on their own or a family member's home, not in connection with a business, is a domestic client.

scope: builder; not stated; small domestic building site
rules: A site must have readily accessible toilets that are clean, lit and ventilated.
Washing facilities with running hot and cold or warm water, soap and towels must be provided next to the toilets.
Drinking water, changing and drying facilities where special work clothing is worn, and rest facilities with tables, chairs with backs and the means to boil water and prepare food must be provided.

scope: decorator or builder; not stated; two days painting soffits and fascias on a two storey semi-detached house
rules: A ladder may be used for work at height only where a risk assessment shows more suitable equipment is not justified because the risk is low and the use is short, or because of site features that cannot be changed.
Short duration means roughly 15 to 30 minutes in one position for light work.
Collective protection such as a tower or scaffold must be chosen in preference to personal protection.

scope: not stated; not stated; use of ladders on building sites
rules: Ladders are not banned; a ladder may be used where a risk assessment shows the risk is low and the use is short or site features cannot be changed.
A ladder in use must be secured against slipping.

scope: roofer or builder; not stated; replacing a few slipped tiles on a pitched roof
rules: For short-duration work on a pitched roof, decided by a risk assessment, the minimum is safe access to roof level plus a purpose-made, supported roof ladder.
The roof ladder should span at least three rafters and be secured over the ridge by a proper anchorage, not by bearing on the ridge tiles.

scope: employer; not stated; workers using breakers for hours
rules: For hand-arm vibration the daily exposure action value is 2.5 m/s² A(8) and the exposure limit value, which must not be exceeded, is 5 m/s² A(8).
In the points system, 100 points a day equals the action value and 400 points the limit value.
Workers exposed at or above the action value, or otherwise at risk, must be under health surveillance.

scope: employer; not stated; choosing ear defenders
rules: Hearing protection must be chosen to bring exposure below the exposure limit values.
Hearing protection should aim for 70 to 80 dB(A) at the ear and avoid bringing levels below 70 dB(A), because over-protection stops people hearing warnings and each other.

scope: builder; not stated; digging footings near buried cables and gas pipes
rules: Work that could strike buried services must not start until suitable precautions are taken, such as getting service plans, locating services with a cable avoidance tool and marking the route.
Mechanical excavators and power tools should not be used within 0.5 m of the suspected line of a buried service.

scope: builder; not stated; chasing a wall near a circuit said to be switched off
rules: Precautions such as locking off must be taken to stop isolated electrical equipment being made live again during the work.
A verbal assurance is not enough: the isolated circuit must be proved dead by a competent person with a suitable test instrument, such as a two-pole voltage detector checked before and after use.

scope: not stated; not stated; work on live electrical equipment
rules: Work on or near live conductors is allowed only when all three conditions are met: it is unreasonable for the equipment to be dead, it is reasonable for the person to work on it live, and suitable precautions, including protective equipment where needed, are taken.
A person may do such work only if they have the technical knowledge or experience, or the supervision, needed to prevent danger.

scope: contractor; not stated; workers paid as self-employed under CIS
rules: A worker treated as self-employed for tax can still count as an employee for health and safety law.
A contractor must plan, manage, monitor and supervise work done by workers under its control, and an employer must ensure people not in its employment are not put at risk.

scope: contractor; not stated; 1.5 m trench supported with trench boxes
rules: A competent person must inspect a supported excavation at the start of each shift, after any event likely to affect its strength or stability, and after any accidental fall of material, and be satisfied it is safe before work continues.
If the inspector is not satisfied, they must tell the person in control before the end of the shift and give a written report within 24 hours, which must be kept on site and then for 3 months.

scope: not stated; not stated; a construction job (size not stated)
rules: A construction project must be notified if it is planned to last more than 30 working days with more than 20 workers at the same time, or to exceed 500 person days.
Every day on which work is done counts towards the working days, including weekends.
